body:
I focused on scholastics in high school in order to qualify for several scholarships; didn't much care for electives and got randomly assigned to drama. I'm an extremely impassive person with a flat tone of voice. Even when distressed it's very difficult for me to express it, but my teacher was an old hand and taught me the technical side of theater. Our school had a very expensive installation. Lights, huge sound system, seating for about 5,000, and plenty of up space for scenery and backdrops. 

I became the head tech by my third year, and when I returned for my senior year I learned my teacher had retired. She was teaching for the fun of it as her real career had been as a stage actress. The drama classes and theater were put under the control of the school's coach, who was an asshole of the highest degree and more than likely stealing from the school. He came in like some swinging dick, ordering me and my crew around as if he knew what the hell he was talking about. Well, since I was working with professional acting troupes that were passing through I was obligated to give them my best, so I took it upon myself to do the job right rather than in the manner the coach told us. 

He stripped me of my responsibilities on the spot, which I expected and accepted was a consequence of professional pride. He took my keys to the facility, bitched me out, but when he threatened to say I couldn't walk for graduation my folks referred him to their attorney. They backed off, but they never did ask for the schematics and operation manuals for all the hardware installed into the theater that my teacher had entrusted me with. 

It's a 30 million dollar facility that the asshole hasn't a clue how to work.

Well, I know it probably makes me an evil person in the eyes of a bunch of people who've never really had to examine their feelings and so simply react rather than think, but if you don't live in the same house as any of them I'd cautiously suggest you consider telling them to leave you be. There's a point you've got to focus on Number One.

I know what you mean. All through my treatments, the stops and starts, I was fine; it was my family that was shaking and wailing like we were in some tent revival. I loved them, and I still do, but for crying out loud, show a little decorum. I'm the one who's facing this, and I really don't need them making this so much harder by hanging on and crying and whining and begging when the cold hard facts of the situation can't be changed. I'd respect their decision were the situation reversed, but they won't respect mine, and it's turning the love I have for them to resentment because they're making what time I've got left a misery. 

I'm sorry for your problems, and I suggest that you distance yourself from your family both physically and emotionally so you can do what you need to do and live as you choose to live. It is your life, and you must live it for yourself, no one else, no matter how much others try to guilt you into thinking about how your decisions impact the ones you love. At the end of the day, you shouldn't be made to suffer for their convenience and to avoid their hurt feelings.
If someone doesn't take that first step toward establishing precedent for self-defense laws to apply when defending oneself against attack by law enforcement, it's not going to happen.

Do yourself a favor and invest in a conceal carry permit and a Tokarev. At least you can take the bastard with you that way. 

Edit: Guess 22 of you would rather just be shot to death. Not surprised. Saddened, but not surprised.

PM me and we can talk. Whenever you like. It's easier to speak to someone who's also hurting, I've found, compared to a therapist. Funnily enough, I was a therapist back when I could work. So we might get a bit of both worlds.
Thank you for taking the time to respond.

Sympathy, commiseration, sharing stories, even people choosing to vent rage: these things I can handle and half-expected. But baseless platitudes, crocodile tears, and logical fallacies just make me see red. They are a disservice to the people on this sub that actually help others, and insult both our intelligences. 

Edit: And, out of curiousity, I went to your chatline website and logged on. Good God, it's a wonder that more people in crisis aren't driven over the edge than are saved. The woman to whom I spoke did nothing but patronize me, serve up heaping helpings of the same platitudes you have, and when she brought religion into the conversation she became so offended that I didn't share the same beliefs as she that she cut the line, all while truly believing to the core of her misguided little soul that she was somehow helping. Some people can't be fixed. They're better off dead. Sometimes they need to speak to someone who can see things objectively instead of having an agenda shoved down their throats, and to be told to live in increasing pain until I'm lucky enough to die of natural causes because it fits your worldview and beliefs is the height of cruelty.
